prompt: Name a play by William Shakespeare

answers.name: Romeo and Juliet
answers.fact: Set in Verona, where tourists still leave letters for Juliet.

answers.name: Hamlet
answers.fact: Shakespeare's longest play.

answers.name: Macbeth
answers.fact: Actors call it 'the Scottish play' to dodge bad luck.

answers.name: Othello
answers.fact: Gave us 'the green-eyed monster' for jealousy.

answers.name: King Lear
answers.fact: A king carves up his kingdom by asking which daughter loves him most.

answers.name: A Midsummer Night's Dream
answers.fact: Bottom ends up with a donkey's head.

answers.name: The Tempest
answers.fact: Thought to be the last play he wrote on his own.

answers.name: Julius Caesar
answers.fact: 'Et tu, Brute?'

answers.name: Much Ado About Nothing
answers.fact: Beatrice and Benedick bicker their way to love.

answers.name: Titus Andronicus
answers.fact: His bloodiest play, featuring a pie you'd rather not eat.

answers.name: Twelfth Night
answers.fact: Named after the last night of the Christmas season.

answers.name: The Merchant of Venice
answers.fact: Shylock demands 'a pound of flesh'.

answers.name: As You Like It
answers.fact: 'All the world's a stage' comes from it.

answers.name: The Taming of the Shrew
answers.fact: Inspired 10 Things I Hate About You.

answers.name: Richard III
answers.fact: 'A horse! A horse! My kingdom for a horse!'

answers.name: Henry V
answers.fact: Home of the 'band of brothers' speech.

answers.name: Antony and Cleopatra
answers.fact: Gave us 'salad days'.

answers.name: The Winter's Tale
answers.fact: Features the stage direction 'Exit, pursued by a bear'.

answers.name: The Comedy of Errors
answers.fact: His shortest play, with two sets of identical twins.

answers.name: Coriolanus
answers.fact: A Roman general too proud to beg for votes.

answers.name: Henry IV
answers.fact: Introduced the much-loved Falstaff.

answers.name: Richard II
answers.fact: 'This sceptred isle... this England.'

answers.name: The Merry Wives of Windsor
answers.fact: Legend says Elizabeth I wanted to see Falstaff in love.

answers.name: Measure for Measure
answers.fact: A 'problem play' about justice and hypocrisy.

answers.name: All's Well That Ends Well
answers.fact: Its title became a proverb.

answers.name: Troilus and Cressida
answers.fact: Set during the Trojan War.

answers.name: Cymbeline
answers.fact: Set in ancient Britain.

answers.name: Pericles
answers.fact: Probably co-written with George Wilkins.

answers.name: King John
answers.fact: A play about the king of Magna Carta that never mentions Magna Carta.

answers.name: Henry VIII
answers.fact: A cannon fired during a 1613 performance burned down the Globe.

answers.name: Henry VI
answers.fact: Written in three parts, among his earliest plays.

answers.name: The Two Gentlemen of Verona
answers.fact: Features a scene-stealing dog called Crab.

answers.name: Timon of Athens
answers.fact: Probably co-written with Thomas Middleton.

answers.name: The Two Noble Kinsmen
answers.fact: Co-written with John Fletcher.

answers.name: Edward III
answers.fact: Only accepted as partly Shakespeare's in recent decades.

answers.name: Cardenio
answers.fact: A lost play, known only from records.

answers.name: Love's Labour's Lost
answers.fact: Contains 'honorificabilitudinitatibus', the longest word in Shakespeare.
